newsitem.title: ITALY: Witness retracts claims against Italy's Andreotti.
newsitem.headline: Witness retracts claims against Italy's Andreotti.

text.p: A prosecution witness in a murder case against former Italian prime minister Giulio Andreotti told a court on Friday that investigators had put words in his mouth and fabricated evidence.

Gaetano Sangiorgi, a 46-year-old doctor accused of involvement in a Mafia killing, told the court that a signed statement by him had been concocted by two prosecuting magistrates and did not represent his views.
The two magistrates concerned denied the allegations, saying they were the "absurd" declarations of a man accused of involvement in the Mafia.
"They are declarations that merit no comment on my part," said Palermo magistrate Guido Lo Forte.

Andreotti, Italy's prime minister seven times, denies charges at the trial in the central city of Perugia of complicity in the murder in 1979 of journalist Mino Pecorelli, whom prosecutors allege was gunned down by the Mafia.
Andreotti is also on trial in the Sicilian capital Palermo, where he is accused of close links to the mob. Both cases rest heavily on testimony to magistrates by Mafia turncoats.
Sangiorgi, whose father-in-law Nino Salvo was a reputed Mafia "man of honour", told the court that Lo Forte and his assistant Gioacchino Natoli had asked him specifically to talk about Andreotti.
"If you say something about Andreotti you can go home and continue being a doctor," Sangiorgi claimed the Palermo magistrates had told him in a July 1993 interrogation.
"I told them: 'Write what you want because I don't give a damn about Andreotti. I'll sign anything,'" he said.
He added he "told the magistrates I did not know Andreotti and I was not aware that my father-in-law knew Andreotti."
Nino and his cousin Ignazio Salvo worked as tax collectors for the state in Sicily.
They were immensely powerful on the island and were big benefactors of Andreotti's now-defunct Christian Democratic party and had known connections to Mafia bosses.
Sangiorgi is accused of involvement in the murder of Ignazio Salvo in September 1992. Nino Salvo died of natural causes.

In his signed witness statement, Sangiorgi wrote that he was aware that Andreotti and Nino Salvo were acquaintances and that he could not remember whether he had received a wedding present from Andreotti in 1976.
"I never said that," he told the court. "I said that I never received any presents from Andreotti."
Sangiorgi's remarks followed a similar retraction this week by a "pentito", or Mafia turncoat, in Andreotti's Palermo trial.

Franco Filippazzo, the chauffeur of the late European Parliamentarian Salvo Lima who had known links to the Mafia, said on Monday that his witness statement had been tampered with by magistrates who made up declarations.
In his 1995 statement he was quoted as saying that Andreotti and the Salvo cousins knew each other.
He denied it on Monday saying his error had been to fail to re-read his statement after 10 hours of interrogation.
